findings.claim: Reminders for SMS-locked or rate-limited users and teams are now counted as failures and permanently deleted after two cron runs. Before the patch they stayed queued until scheduledDate and could still send once the lock was lifted or the limit reset.
findings.evidence: `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns undefined when `isLockedForSMSSending` is true (twilioProvider.ts:90-95), which hits the new else branch at :178-187. That branch increments retryCount and does not log. `checkSMSRateLimit` throws at the monthly limit (twilioProvider.ts:97-102), which hits the catch at :189-197. It also sets the lock state to REVIEW_NEEDED (checkRateLimitAndThrowError.ts:40-44). The deleteMany at :38-42 then removes rows with retryCount > 1. Reasoned by all seats, not executed.
findings.reason: Raised by all four seats; open-code-review and mattpocock rate it Important. With no spec, treating an admin lock as a delivery failure is an undocumented policy change that silently loses reminders. Red test, not yet run: mock the Twilio provider so scheduleSMS returns undefined (locked), run the handler 3 times, assert the reminder still exists. If this cannot be made red, the finding stays Important and is marked unverified. Open question from mattpocock: whether REVIEW_NEEDED counts as locked in isLockedForSMSSending.

verifier.reason: The SMS-lock half of the claim holds. When a user or team is LOCKED, scheduleSMS returns undefined (twilioProvider.ts:90-95, 144-181), so the new else branch in scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178-187 adds 1 to retryCount without logging, and the deleteMany at :38-42 removes the reminder once retryCount > 1. Before the patch the reminder stayed queued until scheduledDate. The rate-limit half is wrong: checkSMSRateLimit does not throw. At the monthly limit it only sets REVIEW_NEEDED (checkRateLimitAndThrowError.ts:40-45), which is not LOCKED, so the SMS is still sent; only a failed lock-state update (e.g. user.update finding no record because of the `profiles: none` filter at :58-66) would land in the catch.

findings.claim: The catch block now awaits an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update`. If that update throws, the error escapes the for loop: the remaining reminders in the run are skipped, the original error's console.log is skipped, and the handler fails.
findings.evidence: Lines 189-198. Before the patch the catch only logged. The update can throw P2025 if the row was deleted after findMany, for example on booking cancellation via smsReminderManager.ts:251. It can also throw on a DB or connection error, which may be the same failure that triggered the catch. Reasoned.
findings.reason: All four seats agree; all rate it Minor. Red check: mock the update to reject with P2025 on the first reminder, assert the second reminder is still processed. This fails on the pinned code.

verifier.reason: At scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189-198 the catch block awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` with no try/catch of its own, before the `console.log`. If that update throws (for example P2025 because the row was deleted after the findMany at line 48, or a DB error), the error leaves the for loop at line 67. findings.claim: retryCount is read, modified and written back from a stale in-memory value (`reminder.retryCount + 1`, :184 and :195). If two cron runs overlap, increments are lost. Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` avoids this.
findings.evidence: The patch writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. The repo already uses `attempts: { increment: 1 }` in packages/features/tasker/repository.ts:110,122. Overlapping runs are possible with a manual trigger plus the `*/15` schedule.
findings.reason: Three seats agree; all rate it Minor. One-line change to `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

verifier.reason: Both the else-branch (scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184) and the catch block (:195) write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read by findMany at :48-60, not an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so two overlapping runs can each read N and both write N+1, losing an increment.

findings.claim: retryCount is added by spreading the shared select and widening an ad-hoc cast to `(PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[]` at the call site, instead of extending the type and select in getWorkflowReminders.ts. findings.claim: The counter counts failed cron runs, not failures of one reminder, and does not distinguish transient from permanent errors. A Twilio outage or network error of about 30 minutes permanently deletes every unscheduled SMS reminder in the 7-day window.
findings.evidence: The cron runs `*/15 * * * *` (.github/workflows/cron-scheduleSMSReminders.yml). Each run tries every unscheduled reminder within 7 days (:48-60). Errors from `twilio.messages.create` (twilioProvider.ts:104) or missing env (:88) increment the count in the catch. A failure at T+0 and T+15 gives retryCount 2, and the run at T+30 deletes the rows (:38-42). Before the patch they were retried until scheduledDate. superpowers adds an unchecked question: whether Twilio's roughly 15-minute minimum lead time on sendAt causes such failures. Reasoned, not executed.
